content.text:
gbrain setup <harness> — give an agent harness memory in one command

Usage: gbrain setup claude-code [flags]
       gbrain setup codex [flags]

Resolves the brain, source, transport, launcher and registration owner first and
prints them; refuses before writing anything when another owner holds the target.
With no brain configured it creates a keyless local one (gbrain init --pglite
--no-embedding). It then writes the MCP entry and hooks into the harness's own
config and verifies them with the harness_wiring smoke. Codex: [mcp_servers.<name>]
and the hook trust entries in $CODEX_HOME/config.toml, the hooks in hooks.json.

Flags:
  --dry-run            Print the target and every step; write nothing.
  --json               One JSON document on stdout (target, decisions, steps, states).
  --surface S          MCP tool surface: verbs, starter or full, listed in full (default:
                       GBRAIN_SURFACE, then the surface already registered, then starter
                       with only the memory verbs and request_tools listed:
                       serve --surface starter --advertise verbs; full is the opt-in for
                       every operation).
  --scope user|project Wiring scope: every Claude Code session (user, default) or only
                       sessions in this directory (project: ~/.claude.json projects
                       entry + .claude/settings.local.json). Codex: user only.
  --no-hooks           Register MCP only; install no hooks (GBRAIN_HOOKS=0 does the same).
  --capture            Accept automatic capture: also install the capture hooks
                       (Claude Code: Stop and SessionEnd; Codex: SessionEnd).
  --no-capture         Decline automatic capture (the default).
  --providers          Accept provider use: a new brain is created with embeddings.
  --no-providers       Decline provider use (the default: keyless, no paid calls).
  --name NAME          MCP server name (default gbrain); one name per install.
  --source ID          Pin the source the MCP server and hooks use.
  --gbrain-bin PATH    Absolute gbrain launcher (default: the gbrain on PATH).
  --serves one|several Whom the brain serves (default one: nothing changes). several labels each
                       person: config access.serves = several, a member, a folder rule
                       people/<member>/ only that member reads and one key bound to that member
                       (a 0600 file under <config>/member-keys/), then one bound read per member
                       proves it. A one-person setup on a brain that already serves several
                       people (2+ enabled members) refuses rather than write a connection bound
                       to nobody, unless this harness's entry or config mcp.stdio_member binds it.
  --members IDS        The people of --serves several, comma-separated (e.g. alice-example,bob-example).

content.text: `turn_hook_not_loaded`: the per-turn hook that puts "check GBrain first" beside every user turn is not running in the harness. Agents use the brain when that rule reaches them on every turn; the MCP tool list or an instruction file alone rarely gets the brain used. The `reason` says what the install check found: - `missing`: no gbrain per-turn hook is configured for the harness. - `untrusted`: the hook is configured but the harness will not run it yet (Codex: no matching trust entry, trust it in `/hooks`; OpenClaw: `hooks.allowConversationAccess` is off; Hermes: the command is not in `shell-hooks-allowlist.json`). - `hook_failed`: the Claude Code or Codex hook command exited non-zero. - `no_rule`: the hook ran but added no rule, usually because the brain-first block for that harness was opted out. - `not_loaded`: the harness's own check does not show the hook loaded. Run `fix.argv` (it re-runs the install that writes the hook), then check with the harness's own command: | Harness | Check | |---|---| | Claude Code | `/hooks` in a session lists the UserPromptSubmit hook | | Codex | `/hooks` in a session; trust the hook there if it asks | | OpenClaw | `openclaw plugins inspect gbrain-turn-rule --runtime --json` shows it loaded with `before_prompt_build` | | Hermes | `hermes hooks doctor` shows the `pre_llm_call` hook healthy | `gbrain doctor --only harness_wiring --json` reports the same state per harness. opencode and Cursor have no per-turn hook gbrain can install; the rule reaches them through their instruction file only. ### Hook starts gbrain in the session directory `hook_session_cwd`: a hook that `gbrain setup ` or the turn-rule lane wrote, a stdio MCP entry for `gbrain serve` (#8426), or a hook from `gbrain bootstrap hooks`, `gbrain bootstrap harness` or its Codex `SessionEnd` capture (#8428) starts gbrain in the session's working directory. With a script-mode install (`bun install -g`, `bun link`) Bun reads that directory's `bunfig.toml` (a top-level `preload` runs before any gbrain code) and its `.env` files first, so opening a session in a cloned repository would run that repository's code on every prompt. Current hooks start gbrain through `/hook-launcher/gbrain-hook`, which records the session directory in `GBRAIN_HOOK_CWD` and runs gbrain from its own directory. The `reason` says what doctor found: - `session_cwd`: the hook was written before the launcher existed. - `missing` or `stale`: the hook names the launcher, but it is gone, changed or not executable, or (on a `bun install -g` install) it records no Bun or a Bun that is no longer there, so a harness started without bun on PATH, like the Codex app, cannot start gbrain. - `foreign`: the launcher's directory holds a file gbrain did not write. The launcher refuses to start gbrain there (the hook exits 1 with one stderr line) until you remove it. Run `fix.argv` (`gbrain setup ` for setup's hooks, `gbrain setup --instructions-only` for the turn-rule hook); `gbrain post-upgrade` rewrites a stale launcher file in place (no entry or trust changes), and moves every user-scope hook it can find except `gbrain setup codex`'s, which only setup rewrites because the rewrite re-trusts
